Retelling: The LORD told Ezekiel, Thou also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the city, even Jerusalem. And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about. Moreover take thou unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city, and set thy face against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
Discussion: Ezekiel built a toy siege in exile while the real city still stood. Reflect: 1) Why make a model of a siege that has not happened yet? 2) What does the iron pan between prophet and city say about how cut off Jerusalem already was? 3) How do you warn people who believe the worst cannot happen to them?
Significance: A clay tile with a toy siege preached what words had not: Jerusalem's siege was already drawn, and the iron wall between God and His city was already set. Doubt: this is a prophetic sign-act, a staged picture or lived sign, rather than an ordinary historical episode.
RelatedEvents: Ezekiel's Siege Signs; Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile
